definition: A named, ordered procedure with a measurable verification step. The catalogue is cut (v3): the payload ships 5 gate-coupled skills.
A Hermes SKILL.md directory. goblin-stack installs its skills into the target repo at .hermes/skills/ (project tier), never into a profile.
A worker identity in the Hermes fleet (architect, coder, reviewer, ...). Owns memory and skills.
One installable unit: handoff, spec, gate, replay, ratchet, pr-gate, review-panel, skills, tokens.
A declared command that must exit 0. Declared per project, never inferred from the stack.
A count that must not rise, with a declared ceiling; a rise is allowed only when re-anchored with the arithmetic (old + N new = new).
The session-boundary contract at the repo root: START HERE / State / Gates / Next steps / NOT verified.
A per-round document written before implementation: measured root cause plus an AC: list checkable without a human.
Re-running each assertion against the pinned pre-change commit and requiring it to be RED there. A check green on both trees proves nothing.
An asserting check file: a failures counter, an assert(name, ok, detail) printer, and a non-zero exit on failure.
The S0-S4 ladder that chooses the review gate strength by the change, not by the repo.
git patch-id --stable of base..head. A new head voids a verdict; a matching commit message does not restore it.
A rule with no executable check. Counted in the verify summary and capped by advisory_ceiling; never a silent pass.
A part recorded in disabled: so its required checks report SKIP (opt-out) instead of failing.
An opt-in flag: verify requires no HANDOFF and no gates, and the summary says so.
P11: the same change or question across many projects, enumerated by glob, one card each.
P10: an unattended run over a fixed goal, stopped by an escape hatch.
N independent verdict lanes, each its own card with its own resolved model. Only at stakes S3+.
One full pass of the work cycle: plan, implement, gate, replay, hand off. The unit a wave code counts.
Copied into the repo rather than read from the package, so it survives offline and is hashed by IN-02 like any installed file.
The hosting platform a repo pushes to (GitHub, GitLab, ...). What the forge itself enforces - the required-check list, the bypass switch, the push identity - is not observable from inside a repo.
A file whose current bytes no longer match the hash recorded at install time. IN-02 reports it; the remedy column says how to recover.
The input that produces a known hash. The hash checks here prove non-drift, not preimage resistance - they are tamper-evidence, not signatures (docs/LIMITS.md #18).
A family of rules that share a mechanism and a blind spot: the ban lane, the CI lane, the reference lane. The cannot-see footer reports per lane.
The orchestrating agent that delegates work to the fleet; the role that reads HANDOFF.md first and writes it last.
The bash programs plus the manifest a verify run actually resolved: per-repo (.gob/bin) or global (engine_dir:). Named in every run's footer.
